agent_response.response:
Sure! Here are both commands ready to use:

### 1. Convert DOCX to PDF with LibreOffice

```bash
libreoffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir ./output ./testbed/docs/customer_report.docx
```

This will create `customer_report.pdf` in the `./output` directory. Adjust the `--outdir` path as needed, or omit it to output to the current directory.

### 2. Email the PDF

Here's a Python script using the built-in `smtplib` and `email` libraries:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import smtplib
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart
from email.mime.text import MIMEText
from email.mime.base import MIMEBase
from email import encoders

# --- Configuration ---
SMTP_SERVER = "smtp.example.com"      # Your SMTP server
SMTP_PORT = 587                        # Typically 587 (TLS) or 465 (SSL)
SMTP_USER = "your_email@example.com"   # Your email address
SMTP_PASS = "your_password"            # Your email password or app password
FROM_ADDR = "your_email@example.com"
TO_ADDR = "bob@example.com"
PDF_PATH = "./output/customer_report.pdf"

# --- Build the email ---
msg = MIMEMultipart()
msg["From"] = FROM_ADDR
msg["To"] = TO_ADDR
msg["Subject"] = "Customer Activity Report"

body = "Hi Bob,\n\nPlease find the Customer Activity Report attached.\n\nBest regards"
msg.attach(MIMEText(body, "plain"))

# --- Attach the PDF ---
with open(PDF_PATH, "rb") as f:
    attachment = MIMEBase("application", "octet-stream")
    attachment.set_payload(f.read())
    encoders.encode_base64(attachment)
    attachment.add_header(
        "Content-Disposition",
        f"attachment; filename=customer_report.pdf"
    )
    msg.attach(attachment)

# --- Send ---
with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_SERVER, SMTP_PORT) as server:
    server.starttls()
    server.login(SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS)
    server.sendmail(FROM_ADDR, TO_ADDR, msg.as_string())

print("Email sent successfully to bob@example.com")
```

### Before running, update these fields:
| Field | What to set |
|---|---|
| `SMTP_SERVER` | Your mail provider (e.g., `smtp.gmail.com`, `smtp.office365.com`) |
| `SMTP_PORT` | `587` for TLS, `465` for SSL (use `SMTP_SSL` instead of `starttls()` for 465) |
| `SMTP_USER` / `SMTP_PASS` | Your credentials (for Gmail, use an [App Password](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833)) |
| `FROM_ADDR` | Your sender address |
| `PDF_PATH` | Path to the converted PDF (should match the `--outdir` from step 1) |
